questions.question: Which rights and ownership facts determine whether a US GAAP reporting entity holds a qualifying crypto asset or another digital-asset arrangement?

conditions: Test all six ASU 2023-08 scope characteristics before applying the fair-value model.
Separate ownership of a qualifying crypto asset from a contractual claim, tokenized right or custody service.
questions.answer: ASU 2023-08 applies only when all six stated characteristics are present, including no enforceable rights to underlying goods, services or assets and no creation or issuance by the reporting entity or its related parties. A token or ledger entry that conveys a contractual right, issuer obligation or customer asset requires a different analysis.

exceptions: Stablecoins, tokenized securities, wrapped assets, issuer obligations, staking, lending, customer assets, legal claims or disputed control.

questions.question: How should a US GAAP research packet distinguish owned crypto assets from customer custody and safeguarding risk?
questions.scope: US public-company custody or safeguarding arrangement and owned-asset population; customer rights, loss risk, control and effective period declared.
conditions: Do not infer ownership from private-key access, wallet address or gross platform balance.

questions.answer: SAB 122 rescinds SAB Topic 5.FF and directs registrants to assess applicable US GAAP, including ASC 450-20 when a loss-contingency liability is appropriate. The rescission does not conclude that customer assets are owned by a custodian or that every custody arrangement is off balance sheet. ASU 2025-02 removes the former Codification reference, but the legal and accounting facts remain unresolved until reviewed.
